title: These 9 Thunderbird features made me ditch Gmail for good
summary: The underdog with cooler and better features
body: At the beginning of this year, I decided to ditch Gmail for the first time in about 15 years. It was not my plan to let down Google’s email app, as I have always enjoyed features such as Proofread, Confidential Mode, and Undo Send ( this one saved me once when I almost sent an email meant for my wife to my boss). But that does not mean it’s the best option for everyone. Over time, the Gmail app stopped feeling like a tool for sending and receiving emails and became like a marketer trying to sell me Google’s services. From the push for smart features that I don’t need to ads and the cluttered, AI-supported interface, checking my emails became a chore.

title: Are AI Overviews killing websites? A court just sided with Google
summary: This marks the second major setback for publishers in their legal fight against Google’s AI Overviews this year.
body: TL;DR A federal judge has ruled in Google’s favor in separate lawsuits brought by Chegg and Penske Media Corporation over AI Overviews in Search. Judge Amit Mehta noted that the lawsuits weren’t based on a formal agreement with Google, but an “expectation.” This is the second major setback for publishers this year, after a federal court dismissed a similar lawsuit brought against Google. Ed-tech company Chegg filed an antitrust lawsuit against Google last year over AI Overviews and how the feature was affecting website traffic and affiliate revenues. Publisher Penske Media Corporation, known for publications like Billboard , Variety , and Rolling Stone , later filed its own lawsuit against the search giant . A federal judge has now delivered a major setback to both parties. While siding with Google, US District Judge Amit Mehta noted in the ruling that the claims in the lawsuits weren’t based on an agreement with the search giant, but an “expectation” (via Reuters ).

body: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority Meta’s Muse is the latest AI platform to hit the scene, but it’s nothing like traditional AI tools. While Claude , ChatGPT, and Gemini are highly conversational experiences, Meta AI is an autonomous personal assistant that manages your tasks in the background. body: TL;DR Google is rolling out Guided Vision in Gemini Live for blind and low-vision users. Gemini can describe what the camera sees and verbally guide users to reframe the shot when needed. Guided Vision works on Android 9 and newer in markets that support Gemini Live. For blind and low-vision users, pointing a phone camera at something is only useful if the phone can explain what it sees. Google has been building towards just that with Gemini Live for more than a year, first adding visual guidance that could highlight objects on-screen . And now the company is turning that idea into a more accessibility-focused tool called Guided Vision. Guided Vision is rolling out today in Gemini Live on compatible Android phones. Once enabled, users can share their camera and hear real-time descriptions of what’s around them, ask follow-up questions, and get spoken instructions to adjust the camera. Android has always sold itself on one simple freedom that iPhone users don’t really get: the freedom to install whatever you want, from wherever you want. Google isn’t killing that freedom outright , but as of September 30, it has officially started putting a few more gates in the way — and Android users in four countries are the first through them. On certified devices running Android 7 or newer, apps installed through participating stores must be registered to a verified developer. title: A real ChatGPT page is being used to trick people into installing malware
summary: The dangerous part only appears after ChatGPT has already earned your trust.
body: TL;DR Attackers created a fake ChatGPT model called “Plus 5.6” on the real ChatGPT website. It sent users to a fake security check that tricked them into running a malicious Windows command. That command could install malware that could access files, the screen, the webcam, the microphone, and more. There was a time when spotting a sketchy download meant looking for misspelled websites, strange pop-ups, and other obvious red flags . But that gets much harder when the scam starts on a website you already trust. Security researchers have uncovered a malware campaign that does exactly that, using a real ChatGPT page to convince people they’re dealing with an official OpenAI product before redirecting them to a far more dangerous site. Researchers at Huntress (via TechRadar ) found attackers abusing ChatGPT’s Custom GPT feature to create a bot called “Plus 5.6.” The name was chosen to sound like an official OpenAI model, and because Custom GPTs are hosted on ChatGPT.com, anyone opening the link would see a legitimate ChatGPT address in their browser.
